# 1 Enoch Chapter 100 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 100:3 — 'horse shall walk up to the breast'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-horse-shall-walk-up-to-the-breast in-the-blood-of-sinners" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "the horse shall walk up to the breast in the blood of sinners" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Horses will wade through the blood of sinners up to their chests" | Plural; 'wade' for 'walk'; 'chests' for 'breast' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The singular 'horse' and 'chariot' may be collective; LOGOS preserves the literal number. 'Wade' (PNEUMA) is more vivid but 'walk' is the Ge'ez verb.

---

## 100:4 — 'all who helped bring sin down'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all-who-brought-down-sin" | Literal; may refer to the Watchers |
| LOGOS | "all who helped bring sin down" | Formal; 'helped' softens slightly |
| PNEUMA | "everyone who helped bring sin into the world" | 'Into the world' adds spatial clarity |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The phrase refers ambiguously to those who initiated or spread sin (possibly Watchers, possibly human sinners). 'Helped bring sin down' preserves the causal idiom without over-specifying.

---

## 100:5 — 'apple of an eye'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as-the-apple-of-an-eye" | Literal; biblical idiom |
| LOGOS | "as the apple of an eye" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "like the apple of his eye" | Specifies 'his' (God's) |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'as the apple of an eye.' The generic 'an eye' is preferred — the biblical idiom (Deuteronomy 32:10; Psalm 17:8) uses the indefinite form and LOGOS preserves this.

---

## 100:9 — 'in blazing flames burning worse than fire'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in-blazing-flames-burning-worse-than-fire-shall-ye-burn" | Literal; paradoxical 'worse than fire' |
| LOGOS | "in blazing flames burning worse than fire shall you burn" | Formal; preserves the paradox |
| PNEUMA | "You will burn in blazing fires, hotter than anything you have ever known" | 'Hotter than anything' loses the paradox |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Burning worse than fire' is a deliberate Ge'ez paradox — a fire hotter than fire itself. PNEUMA's paraphrase dissolves this rhetorical paradox into ordinary comparison.

---

## 100:12 — Ironic invitation to bribe the rain

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "give-gifts-to-the-rain-that-it-be-not-withheld-from-falling-on-you" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "give gifts to the rain that it may not be withheld from falling on you, nor the dew, if perhaps it will accept gold and silver from you" | Formal; preserves the irony |
| PNEUMA | "go ahead — bribe the rain. Offer it your gold and silver." | Explicit sarcasm; adds 'go ahead' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The ironic invitation in the Ge'ez does not need 'go ahead' (PNEUMA's addition) to make the sarcasm land. The formal construction preserves the original tone more precisely.

---

## 100:10 — Nature as witness — sun, moon, stars

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from-the-sun-and-from-the-moon-and-from-the-stars-in-reference-to-your-sins" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "from the sun and from the moon and from the stars — in reference to your sins" | Formal; dash for readability |
| PNEUMA | "From the sun and moon and stars he will gather evidence" | 'Evidence' for 'inquiry/testimony' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez has inquiry (asking the celestial bodies) not 'gathering evidence' — the legal metaphor of summoning witnesses is subtly different from evidence-gathering.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 6**
